content.title: About
content.content: Macaroni with cheese and tomato is a ready‑to‑eat dish made from short pasta baked in a sauce of tomato puree and grated cheese. It is popular as a quick lunch or dinner, combining carbohydrates, protein and a modest amount of fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tomato sauce gives the dish a rich flavor and provides lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Cheese is often cheddar or mozzarella, which melt to create a creamy texture.
Fast preparation (5‑10 minutes) makes it a favorite among students and busy people.
In different countries the dish has various names: in Italy it is called “pasta al forno”, in the US “mac and cheese with tomato”.
Many variations exist – you can add ham, vegetables or spices for extra taste.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The pasta provides quick‑release carbohydrates for immediate energy.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese is a good source of calcium, supporting bone health.

items.title: Vitamin C from tomatoes
items.content: Tomato sauce contains vitamin C, which helps boost the immune system.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Cheese and optional meat add both animal and plant‑based protein.

items.title: Lycopene
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes has antioxidant properties and supports heart health.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The dish can be calorie‑dense because of cheese and pasta, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Tomato sauce and cheese often contain added salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: Cheese contains lactose, which may cause discomfort for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional macaroni contains gluten; gluten‑free pasta can be used for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, optionally garnish with fresh herbs, drizzle with olive oil or add spices to taste. It pairs well with a fresh vegetable salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. When frozen, it keeps for up to 2 months after cooling and sealing in a freezer‑safe bag.
